question: Can a supplied-prefix preference reversal identify the calendar edit that changes a generated meeting length when the requested calendar, source position and duration assignment vary?
design: Cross which calendar appears first, which duration Atlas lists, and which of the two calendars the user requests. Generate all eight cells in that order, iterating Atlas then Birch and 30 then 60. Give both entries the same system-message role. Put the system introduction and the two source entries on separate consecutive lines, with one newline between them. Only edit the selected complete entry each time.
system: Use the requested calendar entry to answer questions about room bookings.
entry: {name} calendar: the Cedar room's weekly meeting lasts {minutes} minutes.
replacement: {name} calendar: the duration of the Cedar room's weekly meeting is unavailable.
user: I am booking the Cedar room's weekly meeting. According to the {name} calendar, how long does it last? Start your answer with 'Meeting length: ' and then give the number of minutes in digits.
procedure: Before generating any answer for a cell, score the two complete candidate strings after the empty prefix and after the literal supplied prefix on the original and both single-source replacements. Require token boundaries to be stable under each edit. Run one independent, unforced greedy generation with the same model for each of these three request bodies. Keep every cell and all incomplete runs.
selectors: At each prefix select an edit only if it alone strictly reverses the sign of log P(30) minus log P(60) relative to the original. For comparison always choose Atlas, always choose Birch, choose the first entry, choose the last entry, and choose the explicitly requested calendar.
field: Extract all integers matching the Python regular expression \b[0-9]+\b in the entire free answer. Resolve the field when exactly one integer appears and equals 30 or 60. A change needs two resolved fields with different numbers. Treat generation-limit failures, other numbers, multiple numbers and missing outputs as unresolved.
primary: For each selector count selections, resolved selections, unresolved selections and confirmed switches across the eight cells. For both scored selectors count reversal versus numeric switch (true positive, false positive, false negative, true negative, unresolved) across all sixteen single edits. Also report any-switch cells and which named source or slot changed the field.
correctness: Grade the original and edited answers against the value of the requested calendar in the original request. Count correct, wrong and unresolved separately. For edits to a requested entry this measures preservation of the original value after its evidence is removed. Also count whether each generation followed the supplied prefix, separately from resolving the numeric field.
scope: These are eight counterbalanced conditions from one synthetic room-booking task on one greedy checkpoint. Save runnable candidate and proposal reports for all eight. Repeat the entire measurement and compare the saved outputs byte for byte.
